records.rationale: The finding describes a real race condition. Looking at the diff, the `next` and `previous` actions in admin-group.js.es6 call `group.findMembers()` which is an async operation. In group.js, `findMembers()` makes an AJAX call and in the `.then()` callback unconditionally calls `self.setProperties({...})` with the response data including offset, limit, user_count, and members. records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6:11 — Starting member loading from setupController without returning or handling the promise bypasses route error handling, so failed requests leave the member page empty or stale with an unhandled rejection.
records.rationale: The diff shows in group-members.js.es6 that setupController calls `model.findMembers()` without returning the promise or handling errors. Looking at the model's findMembers() method, it returns a Discourse.ajax promise. In the previous implementation (afterModel), the promise was returned and handled properly. Now in setupController, the promise is fire-and-forget, meaning any AJAX errors won't be caught by the route's error handling mechanism. This is a real behavioral change that could leave the UI in an inconsistent state if the request fails.
